6c8f900c37.q: How did Paul Braddock transition from graphic design to accessibility specialization?
6c8f900c37.a: Paul describes himself as a dyslexic designer who got a degree in graphic design and transitioned into UX design. At Co-op Insurance, his team developed a mission statement around serving 'everyone', which prompted him to explore accessibility specifically and conduct user research with charity partners. This discovery led him onto the accessibility path, ultimately forming the Accessibility Champions program with colleague Dave Cunningham.

137075cb4f.q: Has the European Accessibility Act changed boardroom conversations about accessibility at Asda?
137075cb4f.a: While the European Accessibility Act does not directly impact the UK unless Asda trades in the EU, it has been a catalyst for conversations. Asda's George brand does trade in the EU, making it a relevant case study. Paul notes that people are more aware, especially following press coverage and legal cases in France, asking how the regulation impacts the business and individual roles. The EAA has opened doors to conversations about measuring impact on both customers and team efficiency.

4622d8132e.q: Why is accessibility important in retail and e-commerce beyond digital websites?
4622d8132e.a: Asda is more than a supermarket; it offers pharmacy, mobile money, insurance, loans, gift cards, and tire services. Accessibility is vital because retailers must meet customer needs at every touchpoint, especially for vulnerable populations. During the pandemic, many people became dependent on retail and e-commerce for essentials and medications they could not collect in-store. Examples include neurodivergent customers who struggle to remember shopping lists and frail individuals who cannot collect deliveries in-store. Meeting these needs at each touchpoint creates loyal customers.

1d5cb08b8b.a: At every customer touchpoint, Asda questions how to make experiences accessible for everyone. Physical and digital are increasingly overlapping in retail, with customer expectations for consistent and coherent experiences both online and in-store. Paul found this overwhelming initially as it requires considering multiple products and services across different environments. 645971201b.q: What business benefits does Asda see from improving digital accessibility?
645971201b.a: A retail competitor reported significant growth after digitally transforming and improving accessibility of their online shopping through mobile applications. This demonstrates real business benefits to accessibility beyond compliance, comparable to how the fair trade movement grew in retail, similar to the Purple Pound initiative.
